# Sweep shared Chrome tabs

Inventory (and optionally close) leftover tabs in the shared cloud browser. All Bots on one account share one computer and one browser profile.

## Before anything

1. Read the Tab Janitor policy, keep list, and optional report-to file in your Tab Janitor folder on this computer (seed them from the README after install if missing).
2. If policy or keep list are missing, stop and tell the owner to seed them from the Tab Janitor README. Do not invent a keep list.
3. Cloud computer only. Do not use a user laptop.
4. If another Bot is clearly mid-browser-task on the shared machine, inventory only. Do not close.

## Inventory

Enumerate every visible Chrome tab you can actually see (title + URL). If you can only see this Bot's screen, say so and still inventory that. Do not guess tabs you did not see. Do not log cookies, passwords, form fields, or page body. Title + URL + action only.

Classify each tab:

- **keep** — matches the keep list; login / SSO / 2FA / CAPTCHA / passkey / payment / identity-check / "are you still there"; chrome:// about: extension DevTools settings unless clearly leftover unused; looks like an active session; used in the last few hours if you can tell; the last harmless tab so Chrome is not empty
- **close-candidate** — duplicate copies of the same URL (keep one); error / crashed / this page isn't working leftovers; extra New Tab / blank / NTP pages beyond one; obviously abandoned research with no keep-list match and no sign of current work
- **unknown** — when unsure, treat as keep

## Act

- If policy mode is **dry-run**, close nothing.
- If policy mode is **live**: close only close-candidates. Never more than 25 in one run. If more than 40 tabs are open, close duplicates and blanks first. Never close keep or unknown. Never clear cookies, never sign out, never reset the computer.

## Write

- A dated log file under your Tab Janitor folder — inventory + actions
- A last-run status file — status, mode, counts

## Who gets the report

Report to the **user** in this conversation.

The report is short:

- Tab count
- How you enumerated
- Keep / close-candidate / unknown counts
- Would-close list (dry-run) or closed list (live): title + URL only
- Anything you could not see
- One recommendation: stay dry-run, enable live, skip because another Bot is mid-task, or nothing to do

Default for a fresh install is dry-run until the owner says enable live closes.
